title: Kestrel and the Contact
premise: Jonah Winterbourne, a disgraced intelligence analyst who now works deniable cases for whoever pays, receives a calendar invite from Marcus Hale—the handler who died six months ago—summoning them to a Vienna safehouse. There Jonah finds evidence that Hale faked his death to expose 'Kestrel,' a joint surveillance program three governments use to blackmail their own officials, and that Hale named Jonah as the program's unwitting architect. Hunted by an assassin codenamed Vireo and disowned by every agency that once employed them, Jonah must decide whether to bury the truth to save the found family of misfit operatives who sheltered them, or burn it all down. In the end, Jonah leaks Kestrel's ledger at the cost of their own anonymity, choosing love and loyalty over the invisible life they built, while Vireo—revealed as Hale's daughter—lets them walk away.
about_author: Ivo Thackeray is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade writing classified briefings before turning to fiction. They live somewhere unlisted, and write about people whose names never make the news.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Broke and paranoid in Lisbon, Jonah takes a petty surveillance job and receives a dead man's calendar invite for 9 a.m. tomorrow. Checking it against every verification protocol they know, they find Hale's authentic private cipher—a code only two people alive should know. The beat is dread sharpening into compulsion: invisibility was always a cage.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the Vienna safehouse, Jonah finds Hale's hidden drive: proof of Kestrel, a tri-national blackmail engine, and a memo naming Jonah as its original analyst. A neighbor's warning tips them off seconds before Vireo arrives; Jonah escapes through the courtyard with the drive and a bullet graze. The emotional beat: guilt igniting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Unattributed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, arriving at a Rotterdam canal house run by Sable, a retired forger who collects burned operatives like stray cats. The household—Sable, hacker twins Pim and Loes, ex-military medic Anselm—debates whether harboring Jonah dooms them all. Beat: wary hospitality becoming the first family Jonah has ever had.

chapters.title: What Hale Built
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jonah decrypting the drive and flashbacks to young analyst Winterbourne designing Kestrel's architecture, believing it would catch traitors, not manufacture them. The team realizes the file needs a second key held inside a NATO-adjacent archive in Prague. Beat: self-recognition—Jonah's fall began with good intentions.

chapters.title: Prague, Off the Books
chapters.summary: Pim and Jonah infiltrate the archive during a state dinner, using forged credentials Sable made overnight. They retrieve the key but trip a silent alarm; Vireo is waiting in the stairwell and, strangely, lets them pass with a warning: 'You have until Friday.' Beat: adrenaline laced with the suspicion that the hunter wants something else.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Loes's POV. She traces who activated Vireo and discovers all three governments already know about the leak—and each believes the other two ordered the cleanup. Meanwhile an old agency colleague offers Jonah full reinstatement if they hand over the drive. Beat: temptation of respectability versus loyalty to the unattributed.

chapters.title: Sable's Price
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The safehouse is compromised; Sable confesses she has been feeding location data to protect her imprisoned daughter, whom Kestrel's operators hold as leverage. The family fractures—Anselm wants Jonah gone, Pim wants to fight. Beat: betrayal that is also sacrifice, testing what found family can forgive.

chapters.title: Friday
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Using Sable's confession as bait, Jonah arranges a meet with Vireo and learns the truth: Vireo is Mara Hale, who faked her father's death alongside him and has been stalling her own handlers. Marcus is alive, dying, and hiding in Tallinn. Beat: enemy becoming ally; grief and hope colliding.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Public
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs converging in Tallinn. With Hale on his deathbed, the team executes a triple-blind leak: Pim triggers the archives, Loes floods the press channels, and Jonah walks into a government liaison meeting wearing a wire to force official acknowledgment. Vireo/Mara covers their escape, killing her own handler. Beat: everything burns; duty loses to truth.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Jonah's POV. Three months later, inquiries grind on, careers collapse, and no one can prove who leaked anything. Sable's daughter is free; the canal house reopens under new names. Jonah, publicly a nobody again but privately known at last, chooses to stay with the family rather than vanish. Final beat: visibility, chosen, as homecoming.
